title: Billing-cycle boundary metering alignment and auto-heal credits PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers have reported confusing spikes on invoices that occur at month boundaries when metering windows and usage aggregation cut over at different times across services (e.g., application-level counters, deduplicated embeddings, and per-route quotas). Some over-reporting is transient (duplicate ingestion around cutover) and can be safely auto-reconciled. Problem: Current billing aligns strictly to PostgreSQL aggregation batches and job schedules; when jobs drift or a tenant changes timezone/region, a small fraction of usage is either double-counted or delayed into the next invoice. This causes customer support tickets and manual credits. Goal: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a system that (1) aligns metering windows to billing-cycle boundaries deterministically, (2) detects transient duplicate/overlapping metering events around cutovers, and (3) applies automated "auto-heal" credits for safe, low-risk adjustments without manual intervention. Success metrics: Reduce month-boundary billing disputes by >= 75% for customers affected in the pilot; reduce manual credit workload for Billing Ops by >= 60% for the pilot cohort. Scope: - In-scope: defining window alignment algorithm, duplicate-detection heuristics, auto-heal credit rules and thresholds, API/console visibility for pending auto-heal adjustments, and billing audit trail. - Out-of-scope: wholesale changes to pricing tiers, per-token algorithmic re-pricing, and international tax/legal adjustments. Stakeholders: Billing Ops, Metering Infra, Data Engineering, Legal (billing policy), Customer Support, Sales (pilot customers).
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic boundary alignment: For a configurable billing boundary (UTC midnight, customer timezone), metering aggregation produces a single immutable window id so all downstream jobs attribute events to the same invoice window.

Transient duplicate detection: System flags events that are duplicates (same tenant, same request id or same payload hash within a 90s +/- window) and marks them as potential duplicates in a staging table for reconciliation.

Auto-heal credit policy: If the excess usage for a tenant in the final reconciled window is <= 0.5% of billed usage and <= $25, an automatic credit transaction is created and applied to the tenant invoice without manual review.

Visibility: Console shows a per-tenant pending auto-heal panel with count of flagged events, estimated credit amount, and a link to the audit trail. The panel must be visible to Billing Ops and tenant admins (if tenant opts in).
Opt-out control: Tenants can opt out of automatic credits; if opted out, flagged adjustments create a manual ticket in Billing Ops queue instead.

Audit trail and immutability: All auto-heal decisions record the detected evidence (event ids, hashes, windows) and the reason code; once applied the invoice line shows both original and adjusted lines.

Backfill safety: When running alignment as a backfill for historical months, system must provide a dry-run mode which reports hypothetical credits and impact; no real credits applied until explicit Billing Ops approval.

Metrics: Instrumentation for number of flagged windows, percent of credits automatically applied, average time-to-apply, and monthly disputes count; dashboard tile created in Billing Ops Grafana/Looker.
End-to-end test: Simulated tenant with synthetic drift (clock skew, duplicated events) produces predicted auto-heal credits and console visibility in a staging environment; tests must be green in CI.
notes_and_discussion: 2026-02-16 — Kickoff: Reviewed customer cases from Support (INC-2026-145 / INC-2026-189). Billing Ops reported ~45 tickets/year related to month-boundary spikes; primary pain for enterprise customers on reserved capacity.

2026-02-18 — Data Engineering feasibility: Proposed approach: canonical window id = floor((event_timestamp + tenant_tz_offset) / window_seconds). Need to standardize per-tenant timezone handling and daylight saving adjustments. Action: DE to prototype mapping macro.

2026-02-20 — Heuristics discussion: Metering Infra suggested 3-tier duplicate detection: exact request-id match, payload hash match within 2m window, and semantic similarity for embeddings ingestion with threshold 0.999. Decided to start with request-id + hash only to limit false positives.

2026-02-22 — Risk assessment: Legal flagged that automatic credits must be reversible and surfaced on invoices to avoid audit issues. Also recommended retention of evidence for 7 years for enterprise customers. Added to requirements.

2026-02-24 — UX: Console team mocked pending adjustments panel. PM requested two CTA flows: "Apply" (Billing Ops) and "Escalate to manual review". Also added tenant opt-in toggle for auto-heal (default: enabled for trial pilot customers only).

2026-02-26 — Engineering feedback: Proposed threshold $25 might be too low for large customers. Proposal: tier thresholds: <=$25 for < $1k/month accounts, <=$250 for $1k-100k/month, else manual review. PM to validate with Billing Ops economics.

2026-02-28 — Draft PRD posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PRD-54999. Requested review from Billing Ops and Legal. Linked initial spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1187.
Pending items: finalize threshold matrix, add retention SLA for evidence, design backfill dry-run UX, and schedule pilot cohort list with Sales.
